title: Coordinated escalation & handoff for mixed-mode model rollout regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create and validate a single playbook and escalation-handoff template that covers model rollout regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket formalizes a heterogenous-rollout incident path that: (1) defines automated and manual rollback triggers per environment, (2) prescribes an ordered handoff procedure between on-call, SRE, and account leads for customer-facing escalations, (3) provides environment-specific mitigation commands and safe hotpatch patterns, and (4) includes communication templates for customers and internal stakeholders. Goal: reduce mean time to safe rollback and customer notification during canary/model-quality failures.
acceptance_criteria: Single consolidated playbook lives in Confluence with clear steps for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and is approved by SRE and Support
Automated rollback triggers implemented and tested in staging for hosted canary (canary-failure -> rollback) with simulated load
Dedicated and Private runbooks include one-click customer rollback commands and validated preflight checks
Communication templates (Slack escalation, customer email, postmortem template) are available and reviewed by PM and Legal
Two drills performed with oncall + solutions engineers covering both full rollback and targeted pin+hotpatch in Dedicated/Private
rollback_triggers: Generation-quality regression: alert on per-model hallucination delta > 12% relative to baseline (auto-alert)
Latency spike: p99 token latency exceeds SLO by > 3x for > 5 minutes
Resource contention: sustained GPU OOMs or <10% available capacity across a Dedicated shard
Canary error rate: 5xx or malformed response > 2% on canary traffic for 10 minutes
Customer-sourced regression: critical customer report triaged by AE/SE marked 'blocker'
monitoring_checks: Canary pipelines: token-level diffs and embedding drift score
Tracing: end-to-end trace sample from customer request -> model response
KV cache health: miss-rate, TTL expiration anomalies
Autoscale signals: queue length vs. serving thread utilization
Model variant route counts: ensure fallback routes activated
remediation_plan: Triage: collect sample inputs/outputs, ingest into evaluation harness, and compute regression metric
Mitigate (fast): Route affected customer to pinned known-good variant or lower-capacity SLO tier
Mitigate (hosted): Trigger automated canary rollback job (pre-approved) and monitor metrics for 15 min
Mitigate (dedicated/private): Execute documented one-click rollback command (ssh/k8s/agent tool) with preflight checks; if rollback not allowed, apply targeted pinning for the customer ID
Hotfix: If root cause is deterministic tokenization/kernel bug, coordinate emergency PR to runtime with CI gating, then staged rollout to canaries
Notify: Use templated customer communication (see attachments) and internal #incidents channel after mitigation start
Postmortem: Owner assigned within 24h, include RCA, detection/mitigation timeline, and follow-ups
runbook_steps: Step 0: Acknowledge incident and create PagerDuty incident with 'model-regression' tag
Step 1: Oncall collects affected model name, variant, customer IDs, and sample traces; attach to incident
Step 2: Run automated evaluation job from /scripts/regression-check.sh against canary and control datasets
Step 3: If automated trigger met, execute environment-specific rollback command and notify AE/SE for impacted customers
Step 4: If rollback not possible (private/air-gapped), perform 'customer pin' via RPC to route traffic to fallback variant and open concierge escalation to customer's SRE
Step 5: Post-rollback verification for 30 minutes, escalate to full team if regression persists
communications: Slack internal template: '@channel Incident ENG-48270: Model rollout regression detected for model xyz. Mitigation: triggered hosted canary rollback. Customer impact: high. Oncall: Ravi Patel. See incident doc: <CONFLUENCE_LINK>'

Customer email template: 'We detected a behavior regression in the recent model rollout impacting your requests. We have temporarily routed your traffic to a stable model and are investigating. Expected timeline: 1-3 hours. Contact: solutions@example.com'
Status page updates: short summary + link to incident doc + expected ETA for next update
